$comment: Worked example of a disclosure-endpoint response. Shape: one header line + N attestation lines (ordered by seq ASC) + M pending lines, then a trailing LF. The constant-time error response is fully specified — body is exactly 256 ASCII '0' bytes.

body_lines.$note: next_cursor field is omitted when there are no more pages.

success_response.$note: Each line is the JSON encoding of one object (any whitespace style is acceptable inside a single line; the JSONL convention is one record per line). Line separator is exactly LF (0x0A), NOT CRLF.

paginated_response.description: When the chain length exceeds page_size (cloister: 100), the header carries next_cursor and the body contains exactly page_size attestation records.
paginated_response.payload_canonical_rules: keys sorted ASCII ascending; no whitespace; JSON.stringify on the keys themselves (e.g. "fromSeq":101 not fromSeq:101)
paginated_response.hmac_algorithm: HMAC-SHA256 with a 32+ byte secret shared across all replicas of the actor

constant_time_error_response.$note: All failure classes return byte-identical bodies. Implementations MUST NOT vary body bytes, MUST NOT add status-distinguishing headers, and SHOULD NOT vary processing time beyond unavoidable cryptographic timing.
